entries.place: Gravel drive outside the Redmist Estate gate
entries.what_happened: Carla introduced herself to Julian as his bodyguard, inside the Redmist Estate and wherever else he goes, and said his safety was her top priority. She asked to borrow his phone for a threat assessment, saying she would check what was on record about him before the estate's network saw it, that nothing would be deleted or leave her hands, and that he could watch. Julian shook her hand, gave his name, and agreed but kept the phone in his own hand, saying he would unlock what she needed when she needed it. Carla asked to start with login history, then cross-check anyone who had reached out since Bernard's death was made public.

entries.place: Gravel drive and gatehouse of the Redmist Estate
entries.what_happened: Julian opened the login history and found an entry from three days before, after he had booked his train, from somewhere not near the estate; he said he had told no one but his mother he was coming. Carla said someone knew his travel timeline, either by shadowing his booking or through the rail company, and told him to lock the phone but not clear the history. She explained the master key: one passcode Bernard set up that opens every estate lock, accounts, foundation books, vault and doors, held only by Bernard and now due to pass to Julian through a procedure run by Jezebel with the lawyer as witness. She said Jezebel did not know about the login yet and was not a suspect, and they would ask her straight about the procedure while keeping the login to themselves for a day. They went into the gatehouse, which smelled of coffee and gun oil and had monitors showing the drive, rear service road and pier gate.

entries.place: Gatehouse and marble hallway of the Redmist mansion
entries.what_happened: Carla advised telling Jezebel the master key needed a review before the handoff and letting her think Julian's concern was new-heir nerves, and said Jezebel's office was in the east wing. Julian agreed and said that if Jezebel's account of the procedure did not match what Carla remembered, that would be her cue to speak, not his; Carla agreed. In the marble hallway Gabriella, dressed in a lavender gown and pearls, stepped out and offered to show Julian the house, calling Carla his minder. Julian declined, saying he had business with Jezebel about finances and paperwork first and would walk the house on his own time. Gabriella warned him the east wing had a draft, said she would be in the west parlor that afternoon, and went upstairs. Carla said there was no draft in the east wing and that it was a warning to keep him away from something.

entries.place: East wing hallway of the Redmist mansion
entries.what_happened: Julian told Carla they would not investigate Gabriella's warning that day, but he wanted to learn later whether there was a real draft and what Gabriella wanted him not to see. He said that from then on he would play the nervous heir who wanted to see the locks work and would say nothing about the login. He stopped a few doors short of the east wing, squared his shoulders, and knocked.

entries.place: Jezebel's office in the east wing
entries.what_happened: Jezebel let Julian into her office, which smelled of ink and old paper and had ledgers stacked along the walls and a window on the formal gardens. Julian said he wanted to understand the accounts and foundations and to see the master-key handoff end to end before setting a new code, admitting he was new to it and worried. Jezebel described the handoff: the vault room off the old dispensary, lawyer Campion and Jezebel as witnesses, and a new code set from a sealed slip only Bernard had read, destroyed once the new code was in, all in about an hour. Asked who had told him, Julian said an old friend of Bernard's who knew how he thought. He asked whether anyone else had ever handled the slip; Jezebel recalled a retired locksmith who serviced the mechanism four years before and had the slip in hand with the door propped open, a visit she had signed off on. She asked what he feared in that room. Julian told her about the login three days before, from near the estate, before he had told anyone in Islaport he was coming, and asked whom Bernard would have trusted enough to tell. Jezebel named Bernard's dead brother Edmund, Campion the solicitor, and Marguerite, Bernard's nurse for his last two years, who was told things Bernard would not tell Jezebel. She said Bernard wrote everything down in a log in the bottom drawer of his private desk in the study, that she had never opened it, and that Julian might now have cause to.
